title: Why the Central Limit Theorem Matters

scenes.line1: Why do we use normal curves everywhere?
scenes.say: Ever wonder why so many stats formulas rely on the normal curve? What's the trick that makes it work for almost any data?

scenes.label: Sample
scenes.sub: We estimate populations by randomly picking data.
scenes.say: We don't measure everyone. We grab a random sample and use it to guess about the whole group.
Here's the magic: as we take bigger samples, their averages start to pile up near the real mean and form a bell curve—even if the original data is messy.
Without the central limit theorem, our confidence intervals and hypothesis tests could flop. With it, they're reliable, even for strange data.

scenes.question: Does CLT require normal data?
scenes.wrong: Yes, the data must be normal.
scenes.right: No, CLT works for any population if the sample size is big enough.
scenes.say: A common mistake: thinking the central limit theorem only works for normal data. Nope—it applies to any population as long as your sample is large.
